facts.raw_span: recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol
symptoms persisting for 2 years but worsening on admission
symptoms usually occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion and lasted 5-10 minutes
syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
hypertension diagnosed 3 months prior
smoking and alcohol overconsumption (250g/week) for about 20 years
No specific physical examination findings were documented in the case report
High-sensitivity troponin I: 0.01 ng/mL (normal)
Serum potassium: 4.6 mEq/L (normal)
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6
10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA)

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol, combined with ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions, suggest alcoholic cardiomyopathy.
The patient's history of hypertension and ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions support a diagnosis of hypertensive heart disease.

The patient's ECG findings of ST-segment elevations and depressions, combined with coronary angiography results showing 10% stenosis in the proximal left anterior descending artery and right coronary artery, suggest acute coronary syndrome.
The patient's symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain after drinking alcohol, combined with a history of alcohol overconsumption, suggest alcohol-induced gastrointestinal symptoms.
The patient's ECG findings of short bursts of ventricular tachycardia support a diagnosis of ventricular tachycardia.
The patient's ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block support a diagnosis of atrioventricular block.
The patient's history of alcohol overconsumption and hypertension suggests a diagnosis of alcoholic hypertension.
The patient's coronary angiography results showing 10% stenosis in the proximal left anterior descending artery and right coronary artery support a diagnosis of coronary artery disease.

The patient's symptoms of syncope and recurrent abdominal pain after alcohol ingestion, combined with ECG findings of high-degree atrioventricular block, premature ventricular contractions, and ventricular tachycardia, suggest alcohol-induced cardiac arrhythmias.

rationales.F01: Recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol suggests a relationship between alcohol consumption and symptoms, which is consistent with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and Alcohol-induced Gastrointestinal Symptoms.
rationales.F03: The timing of symptoms in relation to alcohol ingestion is consistent with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and Alcohol-induced Gastrointestinal Symptoms.
rationales.F04: Syncope occurring only after large alcohol intake suggests a dose-dependent relationship, which is consistent with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy and Alcohol-induced Gastrointestinal Symptoms.
rationales.F06: Long-term alcohol overconsumption is a risk factor for Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy, Alcohol-induced Gastrointestinal Symptoms, and Alcoholic Hypertension.
rationales.F10: High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions are consistent with Ventricular Tachycardia and Atrioventricular Block.
rationales.F11: ST segment elevations are consistent with Acute Coronary Syndrome and Coronary Artery Disease, but also with Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy.
